title: Composite-level aggregation in rotation curve model selection: A sign-flip decomposition of ∆AIC for SPARC-175
description: Re-fits the SPARC-175 rotation-curve sample with the Kill-Test v6 pipeline and decomposes each galaxy’s ∆AIC into inner (r < rc) and outer (r ≥ rc) contributions to test whether single-number ∆AIC masks regime-dependent behavior. Finds a robust sign-flip phenomenon in 17.5% of galaxies at rc = 3 kpc (16.4–22.2% across rc ∈ {2,3,4,5} kpc) and shows that removing χ2-weighting moves the sample further toward EFC, indicating the issue is aggregation-level, not a weighting bias.

delta_aic.description: Defines the AIC difference used for model comparison; positive values indicate EFC is preferred over NFW.

v_efc.description: EFC rotation-curve template with parameters v_flat, r_turnon, and p (k_EFC = 3).

v_nfw.description: NFW circular velocity profile expressed in terms of V200, concentration c, and r200 (k_NFW = 2; H0 = 67.4 km s^{-1} Mpc^{-1}).

aic_inner_outer.description: Heuristic decomposition of ∆AIC into inner and outer radial contributions evaluated at the global best-fit parameters; w_i = 1/\sigma_i^2 unless otherwise stated.

aic_consistency.description: Consistency relation linking the inner/outer decomposition back to the global ∆AIC.

sign_flip_condition.description: Defines a sign-flip: the model preferred globally is disfavoured by outer points alone.

key_results.main_finding: At rc = 3 kpc, 17.5% (30/171) of SPARC galaxies exhibit a sign-flip between global and outer-only ∆AIC, robustly 16.4–22.2% across rc ∈ {2,3,4,5} kpc; removing χ2-weighting increases EFC wins (66.7% → 86.5%), indicating the issue is aggregation-level, not a weighting bias.

sealed_predictions.statement: Applying the same inner/outer ∆AIC decomposition (rc ∈ {2,3,4,5} kpc) to an independent, SPARC-quality rotation-curve sample will yield a sign-flip rate in the 15–25% range.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Re-fitting an independent rotation-curve dataset with persisted per-point model curves and computing sign-flip rates across the specified rc grid.

kill_criteria: KC1: If independent subset refits on r < rc and r ≥ rc (with proper uncertainty propagation) reduce the sign-flip rate below 5% across rc ∈ {2,3,4,5} kpc with bootstrap-consistent errors, the aggregation-level misclassification claim is falsified.

KC2: If switching from 1/σ^2 weights to uniform weights decreases the global EFC win fraction by ≥10 percentage points relative to standard weighting (contrary to the observed increase from 66.7% to 86.5%), the reweighting result in this paper is falsified.

KC3: If correcting for known systematics (e.g., beam smearing, distances, inclinations) on the same galaxies yields ≥90% agreement between global and outer-only ∆AIC signs across rc ∈ {2,3,4,5} kpc, the necessity of composite-level aggregation is refuted.

KC4: If the persisted per-point model curves do not reproduce the recomputed global ∆AIC within numerical tolerance, the validity of the inner/outer decomposition as a contribution analysis is invalidated.

KC5: Model-level (EFC) kill: If for the majority of galaxies (≥80%), ∆AIC_outer(rc) ≤ −10 at r ≥ rc and simultaneously ∆AIC_inner(rc) ≤ 0 for the same rc, then EFC is disfavoured in both regimes and fails this empirical test.
